To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phosphatase, PTEN, is a novel mediator of leptin signalling in hypothalamic cells and pancreatic β‐ cells, and that PTEN inhibition is a key mechanism underlying the differential cellular effects of insulin and leptin.
leptin‐induced F‐actin disassembly in mouse hypothalami and pancreatic β‐cell lines requires PTEN inhibition.
1) leptin stimulates F‐actin polymerization in hypothalamic cells, and 2) this effect of leptin requires the lipid phosphatase activity of PTEN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PTEN in the control of cell polarity, migration, growth and proliferation.
the role of PTEN and the phosphoinositide 3-kinase pathway in leptin and glucose homeostasis.
the role of leptin in the regulation of body weight and metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effects of leptin and insulin are mediated by the PI3‐K signalling pathway and that PTEN acts as a negative regulator of leptin and possibly insulin signalling in the hypothalamus and pancreatic β‐cell.
leptin signalling is mediated by PTEN inhibition in the hypothalamus and pancreatic beta cells.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
leptin can stimulate F-actin depolymentization and PTEN inactivation via a PI3-kinase dependent mechanism.
the leptin‐induced inhibition of the phosphatase activity of PTEN in hypothalamic cells and pancreatic β‐ cells is a novel mechanism for the regulation of the leptin signalling pathway.
we have identified a new signalling pathway for leptin that is dependent on PTEN.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phosphatase activity of PTEN is critical for the regulation of the PI3K pathway in the hypothalamus.
leptin can inhibit PTEN activity, and that this inhibition is important for the ability of leptin to stimulate F‐actin disassembly and downstream signalling in the hypothalamus.
the PI3‐K/Akt pathway is not the only way in which leptin can exert its effects in the CNS.
